text:
maya: Drafting the PRD for Dedicated Capacity SLA + launch gates. Pulling together acceptance criteria, throughput sizing, and autoscale rules — putting the doc here: https://rwd.infer/p/dedicated-sla-draft. Need quick eyes on edge cases (cold starts, multitenant throttles) before I convert to PR.

raj: Skimmed it. overall good. two quick asks: 1) call out 95p vs 99p latency targets explicitly, 2) separate cold-start SLOs from steady-state SLOs. also add how we measure 'request' for batching (tokens or requests).

lina: +1 to raj. also add a mandatory circuit-breaker fallback: if backend queue > 5x baseline for 3m, route to hosted lower-tier model and emit alert. and include per-tenant qps cap to protect noisy tenants.

owen: Autoscale proposal notes: suggest scale-up trigger = sustained GPU util > 70% for 30s; scale-down = util < 40% for 5m; min_replicas = 2 per reservation; max burst replicas = +50% for 2m. include cooldown windows to avoid flapping. also call out expectations for horizontal vs vertical scaling (we do horiz by default).

ana: For quantized vs fp16 variants, throughput numbers differ a lot. I'll add a short table: q4_0: ~12k tokens/s/GPU (batching 32), fp16: ~7k tokens/s/GPU (batching 16). We should use model-variant multipliers in PRD so sizing is conservative. Also include a plan for KV cache warmup — first 10 requests per session may be slower.

raj: Draft acceptance criteria suggestion (short):
- SLA targets: 95p latency <= 150ms, 99p <= 400ms for short chat requests (<=128 tokens).
- Throughput sizing: each reserved pool must demonstrate >= target_tps for 99% of 1h load tests at 75% load (define target_tps per model-variant).
- Autoscale: pass chaos test where simulated 3x burst for 3m recovers to <SLO degradation in 2m with no data loss.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to compatible model variant within 30s when capacity constrained; circuit-breaker trips after 3m sustained queueing.
- Observability: per-tenant tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and an integration test that verifies rollback to hosted fallback.

maya: Nice list. Can we be explicit about measurement windows and statistical methods? ex: latency percentiles computed on p95/p99 of request latencies excluding cold-starts, over 5m rolling windows.

lina: Edge-case we hit before: multi-tenant request storms caused the autoscaler to overshoot because ephemeral burst created lots of tiny sessions; propose a session-aware scale threshold that prioritizes sustained GPU time over ephemeral QPS.

owen: One more operational gate: define recovery SLOs and playbook link. If we fail to meet SLA for >15m during launch day, auto-fall back to hosted region and page SRE. Add this as a launch block requirement.

maya: I'll incorporate all and open a PR later today. tagging @raj @lina @owen @ana for final quick ✅s.

deploy-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-prd/pull/58 :sparkles:

raj: quick nit — add a short 'non-go' list (things we will not support at GA) so sales/customer asks don't sneak in (eg: per-tenant full isolation on day1).

maya: good call. will add a "GA exclusions" section. thanks team, will update and ping again for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
